name: deal-won-to-newsletter-subscriber
replaces_classic_zap: Deal Won -> Add Lead Contact to Mailing List

trigger.trigger_note: Catch hook, posted to by a Notion Deals database automation when a deal is won. `webhook_url` is the one external systems call; `trigger_url` is Zapier-internal and must never be handed out. THIS IS A NEW URL — the Notion automation must be repointed at it or this Zap never fires (see `cutover`).

connection_notes.notion_wf: work.flowers | Dennis <dennis@work.flowers>. NEVER the `Knoxx | Dennis #2` connection (02b95b31-c152-8800-9036-1107e08f70da), which cannot see work.flowers databases.

notion.property_read: Contact Email (rollup over the linked Contact's email)
notion.note: The deal page is re-read with sdk.fetch against the Notion REST API rather than trusted from the webhook payload. A rollup in particular is computed downstream of the relation that triggered the automation, so the payload snapshot can be stale. Nothing is written to Notion.

buttondown.action: ButtondownCLIAPI write subscriber, with automatically_activate: true
buttondown.firewall_finding: Buttondown answers a re-subscribe of an existing address with `This subscriber was blocked by your firewall` (partner_error, HTTP 200) — NOT an 'already exists' message, and indistinguishable from a genuine firewall refusal of a brand-new address. Reproduced live on 2026-08-10 (run 019febef-133f-7f63-b9a7-37864a9c51eb), where it burned all five step retries and failed the run. The workflow therefore looks before it writes: `search subscriber` first (a miss returns `{data: []}`, not an error), short-circuit if found, and only then create. Any refusal that survives that check is real and fails loudly, by design — a lead silently not subscribed is worse than an alert.

behaviour_changes_vs_classic_zap: Empty-payload guard (repo rule). A catch URL is public and gets pinged during setup; an empty body now returns {skipped: "empty-payload"} instead of raising. A payload with content but no usable page id still throws.

Subscribes EVERY distinct address in the rollup, not just the first. The classic Zap mapped the flattened `array[]email`, which on a multi-contact deal would have sent Buttondown a single comma-joined, unusable string.
Re-reads the deal page instead of trusting the webhook snapshot.
Skips (does not raise) when the rollup is empty — the classic Zap's `Contact Email Populated` filter, which halted silently.
Skips when the deal page is archived or in the trash.
Idempotent on a re-won deal: the pre-check finds the existing subscriber and short-circuits.

cutover.status: complete — 2026-08-10, confirmed by Dennis. This durable is the only thing serving the Notion Deals won automation.
cutover.classic_zap_disabled: 2026-08-10 — confirmed by Dennis. Not machine-verifiable: classic Zaps are exposed by neither the SDK CLI nor the MCP connector.
cutover.first_traffic: Run 019fedfe-5f17-7e9a-8eeb-e77f6a67b630 (2026-08-10T23:24:58Z) — the wiring-up test click, delivering {"querystring":{}}. Returned {skipped: "empty-payload"} and did NOT raise, which is the empty-payload guard doing its job in production. No real won-deal event has reached it yet.
